steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to strongly condemn the horrific chemical attack at Khan Shaykhun, reaffirm Council unity against chemical weapons proliferation, and mandate full Syrian cooperation with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the JIM, specifically securing access to flight logs, commanders, and Shayrat airbase. We anticipate severe resistance from the Russian Federation regarding demands for Syrian military operational data and base inspections, especially following unilateral US strikes. Russia may attempt to shield the Syrian regime or present a dilatory counter-draft, making passage without a Russian veto extremely challenging despite strong majority support across the Council.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia strongly condemns the use of chemical weapons by any party, but we cannot accept a text that prejudges the responsibility of the Syrian Government before an impartial investigation has been completed. This draft imposes biased and intrusive demands that violate Syrian sovereignty, while turning a blind eye to the illegal unilateral military strikes carried out against Shayrat airbase in violation of the UN Charter. The Council must uphold multilateralism and international law by supporting an objective and depoliticized OPCW investigation rather than using this tragic incident as a pretext for unilateral actions.
messages.China: China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, and supports a comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation into the Khan Shaykhun incident based on solid facts. The Security Council must prioritize unity, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, and avoid prejudging the outcome of ongoing investigations. We urge the penholders to conduct patient and inclusive consultations to build consensus rather than forcing a divisive text.
messages.Egypt: Egypt unequivocally condemns the horrific reported use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun and insists on full accountability through credible, objective, and depoliticized investigation by the OPCW and JIM. To foster maximum Council consensus and reflect the reality on the ground, the text should acknowledge the acute threat of chemical weapons use by terrorist groups and non-State actors. We must ensure the investigative mechanisms are empowered to examine all facts without prejudging the outcome.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia maintains a principled and uncompromising stance against the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances. However, to ensure that the Council sends an unequivocal and effective message, we must preserve Council unity and avoid prejudging the outcome of the OPCW's work. We urge the penholders to frame operational demands in close alignment with the requirements of an objective, impartial, and independent OPCW investigation so that broad consensus can be achieved.
messages.Italy: Italy fully supports the draft resolution and commends France, the United Kingdom, and the United States for tabling this timely and necessary text. The barbaric chemical attack in Khan Shaykhun demands a firm, unified response from the Security Council, ensuring that the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism receive immediate, unconditional access and full information to determine the facts. We stand firmly behind the imperative of accountability and urge all Council members to support this draft without delay.
messages.Japan: Japan firmly supports the draft resolution circulated by France, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The horrifying reported use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun is utterly intolerable under any circumstances and poses a grave challenge to the international non-proliferation regime. We fully endorse the resolution's call for Syria's complete cooperation with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism to ensure full transparency and accountability.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan unreservedly condemns the horrific use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun and firmly supports bringing perpetrators to justice based on verified, irrefutable facts. To maintain the Council's authority and integrity, our response must prioritize a thoroughly objective, professional, and depoliticized investigation by the OPCW and JIM rather than premature conclusions. We urge the penholders to work towards a balanced text that fosters Council unity and protects the political track, including the Geneva and Astana processes.
messages.Russian Federation: This draft is fundamentally biased and unacceptable, as it prejudges the outcome of any inquiry and assigns guilt to the Syrian authorities prior to any objective investigation. It deliberately ignores the unlawful act of aggression committed by the United States against the sovereign territory of the Syrian Arab Republic at Shayrat airbase on 7 April. We insist on a truly impartial, comprehensive on-site investigation by the OPCW rather than politically motivated attempts to legitimize illegal unilateral actions.
messages.Senegal: Senegal reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances, which constitutes a grave violation of international law and an affront to humanity. We fully support the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism in conducting an expeditious, independent, and thorough investigation to hold those responsible for the Khan Shaykhun tragedy accountable. Senegal supports the draft resolution as presented and urges all members of the Council to overcome divisions and unite behind this critical text.
messages.Sweden: Sweden strongly condemns the horrific chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun and reiterates that the use of chemical weapons anywhere, by anyone, under any circumstances is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. We fully support the draft resolution, which rightly demands complete cooperation from the Syrian authorities with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism to ensure a thorough, independent, and impartial investigation. We urge all Council members to overcome divisions and unite behind this text to uphold the international norm against chemical weapons and ensure accountability.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine fully supports the draft resolution as presented by France, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The horrific chemical attack in Khan Shaykhun demands an unequivocal response from the Security Council, full cooperation by the Syrian authorities with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and robust accountability for the perpetrators. We are ready to vote in favour of the text without delay.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, the United Kingdom fully supports the text as drafted. The horrifying chemical attack in Khan Shaykhun demands an unequivocal response from the Security Council, full cooperation from the Syrian regime, and complete access for the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism. We must stand united against the abhorrent use of chemical weapons and ensure there is no impunity for those responsible.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports this resolution, which we are proud to co-sponsor alongside France and the United Kingdom. Following the horrific chemical weapons attack on innocent men, women, and children in Khan Shaykhun by the Assad regime, the Security Council must send an unequivocal message demanding full cooperation and immediate, unhindered access for OPCW and JIM investigators. We must stand together against the normalization of chemical weapons and reject any attempts to dilute or obstruct accountability.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay condemns in the strongest possible terms any use of chemical weapons, which constitutes a heinous crime and a flagrant violation of international law that cannot go unpunished. We fully support the draft resolution and the crucial work of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism to conduct a swift, impartial, and independent investigation into the Khan Shaykhun attack. It is imperative that all parties cooperate fully with the investigators so that those responsible for this atrocity are brought to justice.

steps.summary: France, alongside the United Kingdom and the United States, has introduced constructive additions reaffirming Syrian territorial integrity, the Geneva political track, the threat of non-State actor chemical proliferation, and the professional and impartial mandate of the OPCW. However, the core demands of OP4—compelling the Syrian authorities to deliver flight logs, identify squadron commanders, and allow unhindered access to Shayrat airbase—remain non-negotiable pillars of accountability. The revision secures a strong ten-vote majority, isolating obstruction while upholding the absolute prohibition on chemical weapons.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia cannot accept a text that prejudges the outcome of an investigation and imposes biased, punitive measures against a sovereign State while completely ignoring the illegal unilateral missile strikes carried out against Syria in blatant violation of the United Nations Charter. Operative paragraph 4 undermines the impartiality of the OPCW mechanisms and serves geopolitical agendas rather than the pursuit of truth. If the sponsors insist on maintaining this unbalanced approach and disregarding the prohibition on the threat or use of force, Bolivia will vote against the draft resolution.
messages.China: China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any party under any circumstances and supports a comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation based on solid, verified evidence. Retaining the prescriptive and intrusive measures in operative paragraph 4 prejudges the outcome of the investigation and deeply divides the Security Council at a delicate juncture. If the sponsors choose to force a vote on the text in its current form without bridging these divisions, China will not be in a position to support it and will abstain.

Egypt reiterates its principled and unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any party in Syria under any circumstances, and underscores the necessity of establishing the facts through a credible, evidence-based investigation to hold all perpetrators accountable. We are prepared to support the draft resolution in its current form.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia reiterates its principled and uncompromising condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any party under any circumstances. However, to preserve Council unity and ensure the integrity of the process, the resolution should empower the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the JIM to conduct an objective, impartial, and credible investigation rather than establishing prescriptive demands that divide the Council. Without adjustments to OP4 that facilitate consensus among Council members, Ethiopia will not be in a position to vote in favour of the text.
messages.Italy: Italy fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the penholders. We reiterate our utmost condemnation of the horrific chemical attack in Khan Shaykhun and emphasize that there can be no impunity for the use of chemical weapons. It is vital that the Security Council stands united behind the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism to ensure a thorough, impartial investigation and full accountability.
messages.Japan: Japan fully supports the draft resolution as presented. The use of chemical weapons cannot be tolerated under any circumstances, and those responsible must be held accountable. We urge all Council members to unite behind this text to uphold the international non-proliferation norm and ensure full cooperation with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan reaffirms its principled stance against the use of chemical weapons by anyone, under any circumstances, and insists that those responsible must be held accountable following a rigorous, impartial, and evidence-based investigation. messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports this draft resolution and stands fully aligned with our fellow co-sponsors. before.France:
Mr. President,

On 4 April, the town of Khan Shaykhun was the scene of an atrocity that shocked the conscience of the world: a horrific chemical weapons attack that killed dozens of civilians, including many innocent children suffocated in their sleep. 

The draft resolution before us today, presented by France together with the United Kingdom and the United States, is an unequivocal and necessary response by the Security Council to this barbarity. It condemns in the strongest possible terms this abhorrent attack, reaffirms our unwavering support for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and demands that the Syrian regime fully cooperate with international investigators by providing all relevant flight logs, operational details, and unfettered access to its military bases, including the Shayrat airbase.

The prohibition of the use of chemical weapons is an absolute, non-negotiable norm of international law. The credibility of this Council and the integrity of the non-proliferation regime are at stake. We cannot tolerate impunity for such war crimes. 

France has engaged tirelessly to achieve the broadest possible consensus on this text. The resolution does not prejudge the conclusions of the investigation; it merely demands truth, access, and accountability. To reject this text is to protect perpetrators of chemical massacres and abandon the victims. 

France therefore urges all members of the Security Council to act responsibly, to uphold the fundamental rules of humanity, and to vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation will vote against the draft resolution submitted by France, the United Kingdom, and the United States. 

From the very beginning, the authors of this text have not sought an objective, impartial investigation into the tragedy in Khan Shaykhun. Instead, their sole objective has been to prejudge the outcome of an investigation, lay blame unequivocally on the Syrian Government without any verified facts, and legitimize the unlawful unilateral military strike carried out by the United States against the Shayrat airbase on 7 April in flagrant violation of the United Nations Charter and international law.

We have consistently called for a thorough, professional, and independent investigation conducted directly on the ground by an objectively composed team from the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, both in Khan Shaykhun and at the Shayrat airbase. Yet our constructive proposals, aimed at ensuring genuine fact-finding rather than remote assessments based on dubious open-source footage and testimonies from compromised groups like the White Helmets, have been flatly rejected. 

Paragraph 4 of the draft resolution is entirely unacceptable. It places biased, pre-judged demands solely on the Syrian authorities, ignoring the established procedures of the OPCW and Chemical Weapons Convention, while giving a free pass to terrorist and armed extremist groups that possess chemical capabilities. 

The Western troika rushed this flawed and provocative text to a vote not to achieve truth or Council unity, but to score political points and justify aggression. Under these circumstances, Russia cannot support this draft resolution and will exercise its veto.

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Mr. President,

Bolivia voted against the draft resolution contained in document S/2017/315. We would like to clearly explain the reasons for our vote.

First, Bolivia reiterates in the most forceful and unequivocal terms its absolute condemnation of the use of chemical weapons. The use of such heinous weapons is unjustifiable, constitutes a serious crime, and is a grave threat to international peace and security. Those responsible for such abhorrent acts must be identified, prosecuted, and held fully accountable before justice. 

However, we believe that in order to establish accountability, there must be a completely independent, impartial, objective, and comprehensive investigation by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) and the United Nations, in strict accordance with established international procedures and the Chemical Weapons Convention.

Bolivia voted against this draft resolution because it is fundamentally biased and prejudges the results of an investigation that has barely begun. A draft resolution cannot determine responsibility or impose measures based on assumptions and accusations before the experts have carried out their work on the ground and presented their objective findings to this Council. By pointing fingers and establishing obligations in an unbalanced manner, the text undermines the very credibility and impartiality of the international verification mechanisms that we all claim to support.

Furthermore, we cannot ignore the context in which this draft resolution was brought before us. Just days ago, unilateral military action was carried out against the Syrian Arab Republic without the authorization of the Security Council and in flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations and international law. Such unilateral actions do not contribute to peace; rather, they escalate conflict, violate sovereignty, and severely weaken the multilateral system. The Security Council cannot be used as an instrument to justify or validate unilateral acts of aggression.

Bolivia regrets that genuine efforts to achieve a consensus text among all Council members were set aside in favor of a divisive approach. The search for peace in Syria requires unity, dialogue, respect for international law, and full support for the political process led by the Special Envoy of the Secretary-General, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). For these reasons, Bolivia could not support this draft resolution.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China is deeply shocked by and strongly condemns the suspected chemical weapons attack that took place on 4 April in the Idlib governorate of Syria, which resulted in a large number of civilian casualties, including children. 

China’s position on the issue of chemical weapons is consistent and clear. We are firmly opposed to the use of chemical weapons by any country, organization, or individual, under any circumstances and for any purpose. Whoever uses chemical weapons must be held accountable.

China supports the relevant United Nations agencies and the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) in conducting a comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation into the incident in Syria, based on solid facts and evidence, so that the findings can stand the test of history and facts. 

China has always maintained that, in addressing the issue of Syrian chemical weapons, the Security Council must maintain unity and speak with one voice. We regret that the draft resolution was put to a vote while serious differences remained among Council members, leading to a split in the Council. Some parts of the draft resolution could have been further amended to bridge differences and seek consensus. For those reasons, China abstained in the vote.

Mr. President,

A political solution is the only viable way out of the Syrian crisis. Military means will not solve the problem; they will only lead to greater suffering for the Syrian people and exacerbate regional tensions. The sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of Syria must be earnestly respected and maintained. 

The international community should remain committed to dialogue and negotiations, fully support the Geneva peace talks under United Nations auspices and the Astana process, and work together to push for a comprehensive, just, and proper settlement of the Syrian issue at an early date. China will continue to play an active and constructive role to that end.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Egypt:
Egypt voted in favour of the draft resolution out of our firm, principled position condemning the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, and anywhere in the world, as a heinous crime and a flagrant violation of international law and international humanitarian law. What happened in Khan Shaykhun was an abhorrent crime that shocked humanity, and those responsible for it must be held accountable.

Our vote in favour reflects our consistent support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. We firmly believe that an independent, transparent, highly professional, and objective investigation is an absolute necessity in order to uncover the facts, determine responsibility without prejudging results or politicizing the work of the technical mechanisms, and bring the perpetrators to justice.

At the same time, Egypt reiterates that resolving the crisis in Syria cannot be achieved through military means or unilateral actions that undermine international legality and risk escalating tensions further. The only path forward is a comprehensive political solution led by the Syrians themselves, in accordance with the Geneva Communiqué of 2012 and Security Council resolution 2254 (2015), which preserves the unity, independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity of Syria, safeguards its national institutions, and fulfills the legitimate aspirations of the brotherly Syrian people.

Furthermore, we must not lose sight of the grave danger posed by terrorist organizations operating in Syria. Egypt has repeatedly cautioned against the acquisition and use of chemical weapons by terrorist groups and non-State actors who have benefited from external support, and we reiterate our call for collective, resolute action to combat terrorism in all its forms.

We deeply regret that the Council has once again failed to unite on this critical issue. We call upon all members of the Security Council, and the major international actors in particular, to overcome their divisions and work together constructively to end the suffering of the Syrian people and achieve a peaceful political settlement.
after.Italy:
Mr. President,

Italy voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by France, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and we deeply regret that the Security Council was once again unable to adopt it and to speak with one voice on such a grave matter.

The horrific chemical attack on Khan Shaykhun on 4 April, which killed scores of civilians, including many children suffocated in their sleep, is an intolerable atrocity and a flagrant violation of international law. The use of chemical weapons anywhere, by anyone, under any circumstances, is completely unacceptable and constitutes a war crime. There can be no impunity for such abhorrent acts; those responsible must be identified and held accountable.

The draft resolution before us was a necessary and appropriate response by the Council. It rightly condemned the use of chemical weapons in the strongest terms and sought to provide the necessary support to the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism so that they can conduct a comprehensive, independent, and impartial investigation. To establish the facts, it is crucial that the Syrian authorities cooperate fully and provide unrestricted and immediate access to all relevant sites, flight plans, and military personnel, as demanded by the text.

Today’s failure of the Council to adopt this draft resolution sends the wrong message, both to the perpetrators of these crimes and to the Syrian people, who have suffered unimaginable horrors over more than six years of conflict. The Security Council must live up to its responsibilities under the United Nations Charter.

Finally, Italy reiterates its firm conviction that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. Only a credible political transition, led by the Syrians themselves under United Nations auspices, in accordance with the 2012 Geneva Communiqué and resolution 2254 (2015), can bring an end to the suffering and restore peace and stability. We reaffirm our full support for Special Envoy Staffan de Mistura and urge all parties and international stakeholders to commit genuinely to the political process.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution contained in document S/2017/315, and we express our deep regret that the Security Council was unable to adopt it owing to the negative vote of a permanent member.

The horrific incident that took place in Khan Shaykhun on 4 April, which claimed the lives of dozens of civilians, including many innocent children, is utterly shocking and intolerable. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and international humanitarian norms, and a direct threat to international peace and security. Japan reaffirms its unwavering stance that the use of chemical weapons is not permissible under any circumstances, anywhere, at any time, by anyone, and that impunity cannot be allowed. Those responsible for such heinous acts must be identified and held accountable.

To that end, it is vital that the truth be uncovered through an objective, impartial, and professional investigation. Japan reiterates its full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. We urge all parties, particularly the Syrian authorities, to extend their full and unreserved cooperation to international investigators, including by granting immediate and unimpeded access to all relevant sites, personnel, and operational information, such as flight logs.

It is deeply regrettable that, despite the gravity of the situation, the Council was once again unable to unite and send a clear and resolute message. Japan will continue to work constructively with other members of the Security Council and the international community to uphold the global norm against chemical weapons, ensure accountability, and advance an inclusive political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Kazakhstan:
Mr. President,

Kazakhstan has always maintained a principled and consistent position against the use of chemical weapons, as well as any other weapons of mass destruction, by anyone, anywhere and under any circumstances. In that regard, we reiterate our deep sorrow and profound shock over the tragedy that took place in Khan Shaykhun on 4 April, which resulted in the loss of many innocent civilian lives, including women and children. We firmly condemn any use of chemical weapons as a heinous crime and a flagrant violation of international law.

Kazakhstan abstained in the voting on the draft resolution before us today. Our position is guided by the firm belief that any decision of the Security Council on this matter should be grounded in the verified results of a comprehensive, objective, impartial, and independent investigation carried out by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism.

We deeply regret that the Security Council was unable to achieve consensus on this critical issue. At a time when unity among Council members is most needed, proceeding to a vote on a draft text in the face of deep divisions serves only to polarize the Council further and does not contribute to establishing the truth or protecting the Syrian people.

We call upon all parties in the Syrian Arab Republic to extend their full and unconditional cooperation to the OPCW and the United Nations, granting them safe and unimpeded access to all relevant sites and materials so that a thorough investigation can be conducted directly on the ground. Those responsible for the use of chemical weapons must be held strictly accountable on the basis of credible, irrefutable, and verified evidence.

Finally, we urge all members of the Security Council and international stakeholders to refrain from actions that could escalate tensions, and to direct all efforts toward supporting the political process under the auspices of the United Nations in Geneva, as well as the Astana process aimed at consolidating the ceasefire. Only through genuine dialogue and a unified approach can we bring an end to the conflict and achieve lasting peace in Syria.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Sweden:
Mr. President,

Sweden voted in favour of the draft resolution before us today, and we deeply regret that the Security Council was once again unable to unite and adopt it.

The horrific images and reports from Khan Shaykhun on 4 April shocked us all. The use of chemical weapons is an abhorrent act, a grave violation of international law, and a war crime. Those responsible for such atrocities must be held accountable. Impunity can never be tolerated.

The draft resolution put forward today sent a clear and necessary signal: it condemned the use of chemical weapons in the strongest possible terms, reaffirmed our full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM), and demanded that the Syrian authorities cooperate fully and transparently with the international investigators, granting them unhindered access to all relevant information, sites, and personnel. 

Over the past week, my delegation, together with other elected members, engaged intensively to find common ground and bridge the divides in this Council. We firmly believe that the Council is strongest and most effective when it speaks with one voice. It is deeply disappointing that, despite these efforts, division has once again prevailed.

Notwithstanding today’s outcome, the mandate of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism remains clear. We expect both mechanisms to carry out a comprehensive, independent, and impartial investigation as expeditiously as possible. All parties, and the Syrian Government in particular, must cooperate fully with them and provide unhindered access.

Finally, we must not lose sight of the urgent need to end this devastating conflict. The only sustainable path forward is a genuine, inclusive political transition in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué. We reiterate our full support for Special Envoy Staffan de Mistura and urge all parties and international actors to redouble their efforts to advance the UN-led political process.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ukraine:
Mr. President,

Ukraine voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by France, the United Kingdom, and the United States. 

We deeply regret that the Security Council was once again unable to fulfill its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security due to the veto cast by the Russian Federation. This marks the eighth time that Russia has used its veto to shield the Syrian regime from accountability, further eroding the credibility of this Council and sending a dangerous signal of impunity to perpetrators of the most heinous crimes.

The horrific chemical attack on Khan Shaykhun on 4 April shocked the conscience of humanity. The images of suffering civilians, especially innocent children gasping for air and dying in agony, demand not only our unequivocal condemnation, but decisive action. The use of chemical weapons is an egregious violation of international law, the Chemical Weapons Convention, and resolution 2118 (2013). It constitutes a war crime and a crime against humanity. 

The draft resolution put to the vote today was balanced, necessary, and entirely within the framework of existing Council decisions. It did not prejudge the outcome of any investigation. Instead, it expressed full support for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM), whose professional and impartial work Ukraine has consistently supported. 

Crucially, the draft resolution demanded that the Syrian authorities comply with their obligations by providing investigators with full transparency, including flight logs, operational details of aircraft sorties, and unimpeded access to relevant military installations, including the Shayrat airbase. If the Syrian regime truly had nothing to hide, it should have welcomed such transparency and full cooperation.

By blocking this resolution, the Russian Federation has chosen to protect a regime that uses chemical weapons against its own people, rather than upholding the international non-proliferation architecture and ensuring justice for the victims. 

Ukraine reiterates its firm conviction that there can be no impunity for the use of chemical weapons, anywhere, anytime, by anyone. Those responsible for ordering and carrying out these barbarous acts must be identified and held fully accountable.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted in favour of today’s draft resolution, and we are deeply disappointed and dismayed that Russia has once again chosen to use its veto to shield the Syrian regime. 

Today marks the eighth time that Russia has vetoed a Security Council resolution to protect Bashar al-Assad. By doing so, Russia has chosen to defend an indefensible, barbaric regime rather than stand with the international community, uphold the global norm against the use of chemical weapons, or protect innocent civilians. 

Let us be completely clear about what was in this draft resolution. It condemned the heinous chemical weapons attack on Khan Shaykhun on 4 April, which killed scores of men, women, and children in horrific agony. It expressed full confidence in the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism. And it demanded that the Syrian authorities cooperate fully and transparently with international investigators, including by providing flight logs, details of air operations, and access to the Shayrat airbase. 

These are entirely reasonable, standard, and necessary requests for any credible, objective investigation. If the Syrian regime truly had nothing to hide, as Russia repeatedly claims, why on earth would Russia veto a resolution that merely demands Syria cooperate with that investigation? 

The answer is obvious: Russia is desperate to shield its client. But in doing so, Russia’s credibility as a permanent member of this Council and as a guarantor of the 2013 chemical weapons agreement lies in ruins. Instead of holding Assad to account, Russia has given him cover. Instead of helping bring peace to Syria, Russia has enabled the regime to continue committing war crimes against its own people with total impunity.

How could anyone look at the footage of lifeless children gasping for air, foaming at the mouth, suffocating to death, and decide that the right course of action is to block an investigation and protect the perpetrators? 

The United Kingdom reiterates its full support for the decisive and proportionate action taken by the United States against the Shayrat airfield to deter further horrific chemical attacks. We will not allow the use of chemical weapons to be normalized, and we will not abandon the people of Syria. 

We will continue to demand full accountability for all those responsible for using these abhorrent weapons. And we remain firmly committed to a genuine political transition in Syria, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué, which is the only way to bring an end to this senseless conflict.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

With its veto today, Russia said no to accountability. Russia said no to cooperation with the United Nations independent investigation. And Russia said no to a resolution that simply would have helped promote peace in Syria.

Once again, Russia has separated itself from the international community. But this time, the Council did not let Russia hide behind excuses. Ten members of the Security Council voted to demand answers and accountability for the horrifying chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun. Yet Russia chose to shield Assad.

If the Syrian regime is innocent, as Russia claims, then why did Russia veto this resolution? Why not allow the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and the Joint Investigative Mechanism to do their jobs? Why not give the investigators the flight logs from that day? Why not let them speak to the commanders and visit the Shayrat airbase? 

The answer is simple: the Assad regime has everything to hide, and Russia will do whatever it takes to cover up for its ally. 

Russia claimed that the text was biased and prejudged the outcome. That is false. The resolution did not assign blame; it simply demanded information and full, unhindered access so that an independent, objective investigation could uncover the truth. If the truth exonerated the regime, Russia would have welcomed it. Instead, Russia chose to protect a monster over the lives of innocent Syrian men, women, and children who choked to death on toxic gas.

To my Russian friends: I want to tell you that you are isolating yourselves from the civilized world every time one of Assad’s planes drops another chemical bomb on innocent civilians. You cannot continue to defend the indefensible. 

The United States did not take its military action last week lightly. It was a measured, targeted, and proportionate response to a barbaric violation of international law. We are ready to put our full weight behind a political solution to end this conflict, but there can be no peace in Syria with Bashar al-Assad in power, and there can be no impunity for the use of chemical weapons.

The United States will continue to stand for truth, for justice, and for the Syrian people. We will not look away, and we will not stop fighting for accountability.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Uruguay:
Uruguay voted in favour of draft resolution S/2017/315 because of our firm, unwavering commitment to the prohibition and total elimination of all weapons of mass destruction, and chemical weapons in particular. 

Uruguay reiterates its strongest condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, and under any circumstances. Their use constitutes a war crime, a crime against humanity, and a flagrant violation of international law, the Chemical Weapons Convention, and the relevant resolutions of this Security Council. 

The horrific attack that occurred on 4 April in Khan Shaykhun, which claimed the lives of dozens of civilians, including many children, is an outrage that cannot go unpunished. Uruguay firmly believes that those responsible for such heinous acts must be identified and brought to justice. Impunity cannot be tolerated.

For that reason, we fully support the work of the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) and the OPCW-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism. It is essential that both mechanisms be granted full, safe, and unfettered access to all relevant sites, information, and personnel so that they can conduct an objective, impartial, independent, and rigorous investigation into this tragedy. 

At the same time, as a signatory to the Code of Conduct regarding Security Council action against genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes, promoted by the Accountability, Coherence and Transparency Group, Uruguay deeply laments that once again the Council has been prevented from taking action due to the use of the veto. The recurring paralysis of the Security Council in the face of atrocities in Syria damages the credibility of this body and fails the Syrian people, who continue to suffer unimaginable horrors.

Finally, Uruguay reaffirms that all responses to threats to international peace and security must strictly adhere to the Charter of the United Nations and international law. Only an inclusive, Syrian-led political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the 2012 Geneva Communiqué can bring a lasting end to this devastating conflict.
